links.targetTitle: Every reward payment must be recorded against a transaction

title: Every reward payment records its transaction hash and amount into governance Active Data
content:
The payment lifecycle is captured in a single Active Data document. At calculation, A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.1.3 sets `Distribution Reward Payments` Status to `In Progress` and populates "underlying data used to calculate the eligible USDS and sUSDS balances," the eligible USDS and sUSDS balances, and the Distribution Reward Due. At payment, A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.2.3 sets Status to `Paid` and records `Transaction Details/Amount Paid` and `Transaction Details/Tx hash`. At review, A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.3.3 adds Core GovOps' Confirmation and Commentary. The Executive Vote stage then records the reimbursement transaction hash and amount on the Sky Core side (A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1.4.3).

Storing the **underlying data alongside the result** is the load-bearing choice. A recorded amount is only a claim; a recorded input set plus a recorded transaction hash lets any party recompute the figure and confirm that the recomputed figure was actually paid on-chain. Core GovOps' quarterly review is possible for precisely this reason.

The pattern also links the governance record to the chain in both directions. The tx hash points from the Atlas to the settlement; the underlying data points from the Atlas back to the on-chain events the Tracking Methodology consumed. Neither the calculation nor the payment can be quietly revised afterwards without contradicting a published record.

This is what makes the pay-first-verify-later structure tolerable. Post-hoc review only works if the evidence needed to review is captured at the moment of action rather than reconstructed later.
description: The Distribution Reward Payments document advances from In Progress to Paid carrying underlying data, calculated balances, amount paid and tx hash — making each payment independently checkable.
